name: BC847BDW1T1G
title: Dual NPN general-purpose transistors BC846BDW1, BC847BDW1, BC847CDW1, BC848CDW1 in SOT-363 (SC-88)
summary: Two independent NPN small-signal transistors in one six-lead SOT-363 (SC-88) package, meant for general amplifier work. The BC846, BC847 and BC848 voltage grades take 65, 45 and 30 V collector to emitter; every type carries 100 mA continuous collector current. The B and C letters are gain groups: 200 to 450 and 420 to 800 at 2 mA. BC847BDW1T1G is the 45 V, B-group part, marked 1F, on a 3,000-piece reel.

T1 and T2 suffixes ship 3,000 per reel, T3 ships 10,000 per reel. The -NC versions carry the same marking and packing as the part they extend.

operation.text: Q1 uses pins 3, 4 and 5 (collector, emitter, base) and Q2 uses pins 6, 1 and 2; the two share no pin. At 25 °C on an FR-5 board the total dissipation rating is 380 mW and the per-device rating 250 mW.

BC846, BC847 and BC848 differ in voltage ratings: VCEO 65, 45 and 30 V, VCBO 80, 50 and 30 V, VEBO 6.0, 6.0 and 5.0 V. The B group has hFE 200 to 450 and the C group 420 to 800 at IC = 2.0 mA, VCE = 5.0 V. BC846 comes only as B, BC848 only as C, and BC847 as both.
Part numbers that start with S or NSV are the automotive versions, for uses needing unique site and change control; they are AEC-Q101 qualified and PPAP capable.
All versions are lead-free, halogen-free and BFR-free, and RoHS compliant.

The safe operating area plots the largest collector current at each collector-emitter voltage, set by the bonding wire (200 mA), the thermal limit and second breakdown, for TJ(pk) = 150 °C at any case or ambient temperature. The pulse lines cover duty cycles to 10 % with TJ(pk) at most 150 °C, found from the thermal response. The voltage boundary is 30 V for BC848, 45 V for BC847 and 65 V for BC846. At high case or ambient temperature the thermal limit falls below the second-breakdown limit.
Normalised transient thermal resistance r(t) is given against pulse time for single pulses and for duty cycles of 0.01 to 0.5; multiplying by RθJA (328 °C/W max) gives the transient impedance.
